expected_mode_rationale: Service interface over a slice transform with one failing dependency — Light excludes slice/map transforms; no Strict risk trigger (ctx is pass-through, no concurrency, no security surface)
_why_this_fixture: The slice_transform fixture grades a pure function with no dependency, so four of the skill's own techniques were graded only by keyword presence: dependency error propagation, no-partial-payload, wrong-key mapping, and terminal-branch completeness. This fixture is a Service-interface target that exercises all four, and it deliberately does NOT promise a non-nil empty result — so an exemplar that asserts one is inventing a requirement, which `validate_fixture` is designed to catch from the other direction.

hypotheses.description: off-by-one in the range bound drops the last level
a level links to its immediate successor, not to itself — a self-link makes every level look terminal-adjacent and is invisible to a length or ID-only assertion
hypotheses.contract_evidence: Every level links to its successor

hypotheses.description: the repository error is wrapped with %w, so errors.Is still matches it at the caller; %v would keep the message and lose the identity
on a repository error the result is nil, not an empty non-nil slice a caller could range over as if it were the answer
hypotheses.contract_evidence: never a partial list alongside an error

_allow_skipped_cases: Every dependency is a hand-written fake; nothing here needs an environment. A skipped case is discovered, not verified.
